school-c1-english.title: Class 1 English
school-c1-english.description: Every Class 1 English theme — stories, new words, letter sounds and first grammar — with read-alongs, games and tests. Original stories; themes follow the Class 1 English syllabus (Marigold-era units and the newer Mridang book). Topic tags only.

courses.title: Unit 1 · Happy me: feelings and greetings
courses.summary: Talking about feelings, greeting people politely, letter sounds a–d, and writing a sentence with a capital letter and a full stop.
outcomes: Name common feelings and greet people politely
Read and retell a short story
Hear and say the sounds a, b, c, d at the start of words
Begin a sentence with a capital letter and end it with a full stop
courses.note: topic order may differ by edition

scenes.text: Mini wakes up. The sun is shining. She smiles and says, "Good morning, Ma!"
Ma gives her a big hug. Mini feels happy and warm.
On the way to school, Mini sees a little bird. It sings a sweet song. Mini sings too.
At school, her friend Raju looks sad. He has lost his pencil. Mini gives him her extra pencil. Now Raju smiles. Mini feels even happier!

steps.title: Before you read
steps.body: Look at the title. What makes *you* happy in the morning? A hug, a song, sunshine? Talk about it before you read.

steps.title: Read the story
steps.body:
Mini wakes up. The sun is shining. She smiles and says, "Good morning, Ma!"

Ma gives her a big hug. Mini feels happy and warm.

On the way to school, Mini sees a little bird. It sings a sweet song. Mini sings too.

At school, her friend Raju looks sad. He has lost his pencil. Mini gives him her extra pencil. Now Raju smiles. Mini feels even happier!
steps.say:
Mini wakes up. The sun is shining. She smiles and says, "Good morning, Ma!"

Ma gives her a big hug. Mini feels happy and warm.

On the way to school, Mini sees a little bird. It sings a sweet song. Mini sings too.

At school, her friend Raju looks sad. He has lost his pencil. Mini gives him her extra pencil. Now Raju smiles. Mini feels even happier!

steps.title: Solved example: finding an answer in the story
steps.body:
Question: *Why was Raju sad?*

- Step 1: Find the line about Raju.
- Step 2: It says "He has lost his pencil."
- Answer: **Raju was sad because he lost his pencil.**

steps.title: Solved example: what happened first, next, last
steps.body:
Order the events:

- **First**, Mini wakes up and greets Ma.
- **Next**, she sees a bird on the way.
- **Last**, she gives Raju a pencil at school.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Guessing the answer without looking back at the story. Find the line that tells you.
- Reading word by word without thinking about the meaning — read the sentence again as a whole.
- Answering with one word when the question says "why" — give a reason with "because".

steps.title: Talk about it
steps.body: When did you last make a friend smile? Tell someone at home using: "I felt happy when…"

activity.prompt: Put the story events in order

quiz.q: What did Mini say to Ma?
quiz.why: In the story Mini greets Ma in the morning, so she says 'Good morning, Ma!' Bye, sorry and good night do not fit the morning greeting.

quiz.q: What did Mini see on the way to school?
quiz.why: The story says Mini sees a little bird on the way to school. She does not see a car, a dog or a cat.
Raju was sad because he lost his pencil. The story does not say he was hungry or fell down.

options: She gave him her extra pencil
quiz.why: Mini helped Raju by giving him her extra pencil, which shares what she had. She did not run away or sing.

quiz.q: How did Mini feel at the end?
quiz.why: Helping Raju made Mini feel even happier. Being kind makes us feel good.

scenes.text: Ravi draws faces on paper plates.
A happy face, a sad face, a cross face… "Guess my feeling!" he says.

steps.title: New words
steps.body:
- 😀 **happy** — feeling glad and joyful
- 😢 **sad** — feeling unhappy
- 😠 **angry** — feeling cross
- 😨 **scared** — feeling afraid
- 👋 **hello** — a word to greet someone
- 🙏 **thank you** — words we say when someone helps us

steps.title: Solved example: using a new word
steps.body:
Word: **happy**

- Step 1: Say it: happy.
- Step 2: Think what it means: feeling glad and joyful.
- Step 3: Use it in a sentence: *I am happy when I play with my friends.*

steps.title: Solved example: grouping words
steps.body:
Sort these words:

- **Feelings**: happy, sad, angry, scared
- **Greeting words**: hello, good morning, thank you, goodbye

Feelings tell how we *feel*; greetings are what we *say* to people.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Spelling *happy* with one p (hapy). It has **two p's**.
- Thinking feelings are good or bad. All feelings are okay; what we *do* with them matters.

steps.title: Make a picture dictionary
steps.body: Draw and label these words in your notebook: happy, sad, angry, scared, hello, thank you.

items.say: happy. I am happy when I play with my friends.
sad. The boy was sad when his toy broke.
angry. Do not shout when you are angry.
scared. The kitten was scared of the loud noise.
hello. Say hello to your teacher.
thank you. Say thank you when you get a gift.

quiz.why: The smiling face 😀 shows 'happy', which is a glad feeling. Sad, scared and angry are different faces.

options: words we say when someone helps us
quiz.why: 'Sad' means feeling unhappy. 'Happy' is feeling glad and joyful, and 'thank you' and 'hello' are other kinds of words.

quiz.q: Choose the word: Do not shout when you are ___.
quiz.why: 'Do not shout when you are angry' makes sense, because shouting is what some people do when they feel cross. The other words do not fit.
The face 😨 shows 'scared', a frightened feeling. It is not happy, sad or 'thank you'.

quiz.q: Which spelling is correct? (the word for: 👋 a word to greet someone)
quiz.why: The word we say to greet someone is spelled 'hello'. Say it slowly and write each sound to check the spelling.

options: words we say when someone helps us
quiz.why: 'Thank you' is what we say when someone helps us. It does not mean feeling afraid, cross or glad.

lessons.title: Sounds and letters: Sounds a, b, c, d

scenes.text: The sound train stops at station A. An apple and an ant get on!
At station D a dog and a duck jump on. Chug, chug!

steps.title: Sounds a, b, c, d
steps.body:
Letters make sounds.

- **a** says /a/ as in *apple*
- **b** says /b/ as in *ball*
- **c** says /k/ as in *cat*
- **d** says /d/ as in *dog*

Capital and small letters: A a, B b, C c, D d.

steps.title: Solved example: blending sounds
steps.body: Say **apple 🍎** slowly, sound by sound, then say it fast. Listen for the 'a' sound.

steps.title: Solved example: odd one out
steps.body:
Which is the odd one out: apple 🍎, ant 🐜, ball ⚽?

- Step 1: Say each word slowly.
- Step 2: 'apple 🍎' and 'ant 🐜' share the 'a' sound.
- Answer: **ball ⚽** is the odd one out.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Mixing up **b** and **d**. Tip: make a "bed" with your fists — left thumb up is **b**, right thumb up is **d**.
- Saying the letter name ("bee") instead of the sound (/b/).

steps.title: Play I-spy
steps.body: Play 'I spy with my little eye something with the sound…' using the sounds a, b, c, d.

activity.prompt: Sort the words by their sound

quiz.q: Which word begins with the 'a' sound?
quiz.why: 'Apple' begins with the short 'a' sound. Bus, drum and duck begin with other sounds.
'Ball' starts with the 'b' sound. Say it slowly and listen to the first sound.

quiz.q: Which word begins with the 'c' sound?
quiz.why: 'Cat' begins with the 'c' sound. Duck, apple and axe begin with d and a.
'Dog' starts with the 'd' sound. Say 'd-d-dog' and listen to the first sound.

quiz.q: Which word begins with the 'a' sound?
quiz.why: 'Ant' begins with the short 'a' sound. Bat, dog and cup begin with other sounds.

lessons.title: Grammar and speaking: Capital letters and full stops

scenes.text: Ria writes: "my dog is brown" — something is missing!
She adds a capital M and a full stop. "My dog is brown." Perfect!

steps.title: Capital letters and full stops
steps.body:
A **sentence** tells a complete idea.

- It **begins with a capital letter**: *The cat is black.*
- It **ends with a full stop (.)**.
- Names of people and places also begin with capitals: *Mini, Raju, Delhi*.
- The word **I** is always a capital.

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
Fix: *mini is happy*

- Step 1: First letter → capital: **M**ini.
- Step 2: Add a full stop.
- Answer: **Mini is happy.**

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
Fix: *i like mangoes*

- Step 1: "I" is always a capital.
- Step 2: Full stop at the end.
- Answer: **I like mangoes.**

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Forgetting the full stop.
- Writing a small *i* for yourself.
- Putting capitals in the middle of words (caT).

steps.title: Speak and write
steps.body: Write 2 sentences about how you feel today. Circle the capital letter and the full stop.

statements.s: 'the sun is hot.' is written correctly.
statements.why: It should start with a capital T.

statements.s: 'I am happy.' is written correctly.
Names like Raju begin with a capital letter.
A sentence ends with a comma.
statements.why: It ends with a full stop (or ? or !).

quiz.why: A sentence starts with a capital letter, a name starts with a capital and the sentence ends with a full stop. So 'My name is Mini.' is right.
A telling sentence ends with a full stop. A capital letter is for the start, not the end.

quiz.q: Which word must always be a capital?
quiz.why: The word 'I' is always a capital letter. 'am', 'cat' and 'the' are small unless they start a sentence.
A place name starts with a capital letter and the rest are small, so 'Delhi' is right. The others mix up the letters.

quiz.q: Fix "raju has a bat". Which is right?
quiz.why: A sentence needs a capital at the start (Raju) and a full stop at the end, so 'Raju has a bat.' is right.

questions.q: What did Mini say to Ma?
questions.why: Mini greets Ma in the morning, so she says 'Good morning, Ma!' The other greetings do not fit.

questions.q: What did Mini see on the way to school?
questions.why: The story says Mini sees a little bird on the way to school.

questions.q: Why was Raju sad?
questions.why: Raju was sad because he lost his pencil.

questions.q: Which word matches 😢?
questions.why: The crying face 😢 shows 'sad', which means feeling unhappy.

questions.q: Choose the word: I am ___ when I play with my friends.
questions.why: 'I am happy when I play with my friends' makes sense. Playing with friends is something that makes us glad.

questions.q: What does 'scared' mean?
options: words we say when someone helps us
questions.why: 'Scared' means feeling afraid. Feeling glad is happy, and feeling unhappy is sad.

questions.q: Which spelling is correct? (the word for: 😠 feeling cross)
questions.why: The word for feeling cross is spelled 'angry'. Say it slowly and write each sound.

questions.q: Which sound does 'ball ⚽' begin with?
questions.why: 'Ball' starts with the 'b' sound. Say it slowly and listen to the first sound.

questions.q: Which word begins with the 'c' sound?
questions.why: 'Cat' begins with the 'c' sound. Dog, apple and bat begin with other sounds.

questions.q: Which sound does 'dog 🐶' begin with?
questions.why: 'Dog' starts with the 'd' sound.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
questions.why: A sentence starts with a capital, a name has a capital and the sentence ends with a full stop. So 'My name is Mini.' is right.

questions.q: A sentence ends with a…
questions.why: A telling sentence ends with a full stop.

questions.q: Which word must always be a capital?
questions.why: The word 'I' is always a capital letter.

questions.q: Read: "Mini gave her pencil to Raju." What kind of girl is Mini?
questions.why: Mini gave her pencil to Raju, and sharing shows she is kind and helpful. A selfish, lazy or rude girl would not share.

questions.q: Which sentence has TWO mistakes?
questions.why: 'i like my school' has two mistakes: the small 'i' should be a capital I, and a full stop is missing at the end. The other sentences have fewer mistakes.

questions.q: Assertion: We say "thank you" when someone helps us. Reason: It shows we are grateful.
options: Both true and the reason explains the assertion
questions.why: Both are true: we say 'thank you' when someone helps us, and it shows we are grateful. So the reason explains the assertion.

courses.title: Unit 2 · Clean and fresh: bath time
courses.summary: Good habits for keeping clean, a bath-time story, words for things in the bathroom, sounds e–h and naming words.
outcomes: Talk about daily clean habits
Read and answer questions on a short story
Hear the sounds e, f, g, h
Identify naming words (nouns)
courses.note: topic order may differ by edition

scenes.text: Tinu has a yellow rubber duck called Bubbles. Bubbles loves bath time.
Tinu rubs soap on his arms and legs. Lots of bubbles float up. "Pop, pop!" laughs Tinu.
He pours clean water over his head and washes away all the soap.
Then he dries himself with a soft towel, combs his hair and puts on fresh clothes. "Now I smell like a flower!" he says.

steps.title: Before you read
steps.body: What do you need for a bath? Make a list: water, soap, towel… Now read.

steps.title: Read the story
steps.body:
Tinu has a yellow rubber duck called Bubbles. Bubbles loves bath time.

Tinu rubs soap on his arms and legs. Lots of bubbles float up. "Pop, pop!" laughs Tinu.

He pours clean water over his head and washes away all the soap.

Then he dries himself with a soft towel, combs his hair and puts on fresh clothes. "Now I smell like a flower!" he says.
steps.say:
Tinu has a yellow rubber duck called Bubbles. Bubbles loves bath time.

Tinu rubs soap on his arms and legs. Lots of bubbles float up. "Pop, pop!" laughs Tinu.

He pours clean water over his head and washes away all the soap.

Then he dries himself with a soft towel, combs his hair and puts on fresh clothes. "Now I smell like a flower!" he says.

steps.title: Solved example: finding an answer in the story
steps.body:
Question: *What is the name of Tinu's duck?*

- Step 1: Look at the first line.
- Step 2: "a yellow rubber duck called Bubbles".
- Answer: **Bubbles**.

steps.title: Solved example: what happened first, next, last
steps.body:
Order:

- **First** soap, **then** water, **then** towel, **last** fresh clothes.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Guessing the answer without looking back at the story. Find the line that tells you.
- Reading word by word without thinking about the meaning — read the sentence again as a whole.
- Answering with one word when the question says "why" — give a reason with "because".

steps.title: Talk about it
steps.body: Tell someone the steps of your bath in order using first, next, then, last.

activity.prompt: Put the story events in order
items: Tinu takes Bubbles to the bath
He rubs soap on his body
He pours water to wash the soap
He dries himself with a towel

quiz.why: Bubbles is a yellow rubber duck, so the colour is yellow.

quiz.q: What did Tinu use to make bubbles?
quiz.why: Tinu made bubbles by rubbing soap. Sand, oil and milk do not make bubbles.

quiz.q: What did Tinu use to dry himself?
quiz.why: Tinu dried himself with a soft towel. A pillow or newspaper would not dry him.

quiz.q: What did Tinu do after drying?
options: Combed his hair and wore fresh clothes
quiz.why: After drying, Tinu combed his hair and wore fresh clothes, which was the last step.

quiz.q: Why did Tinu say he smelled like a flower?
options: Because he was clean and fresh
quiz.why: Tinu said he smelled like a flower because he was clean and fresh after his bath.

lessons.title: Word power: bath and clean habits

scenes.text: On the shelf: a toothbrush, soap and a comb.
Ma says, "Everything has its place. Put it back after use!"

steps.title: New words
steps.body:
- 🧼 **soap** — used with water to wash dirt away
- 🪥 **toothbrush** — a small brush to clean teeth
- 🧺 **towel** — a cloth to dry yourself
- 🪮 **comb** — a tool to tidy hair
- 🛁 **bath** — washing the whole body
- 💧 **water** — a clear liquid we drink and wash with

steps.title: Solved example: using a new word
steps.body:
Word: **soap**

- Step 1: Say it: soap.
- Step 2: Think what it means: used with water to wash dirt away.
- Step 3: Use it in a sentence: *Wash your hands with soap.*

steps.title: Solved example: grouping words
steps.body:
Sort by use:

- **For teeth**: toothbrush, toothpaste
- **For body**: soap, water, towel
- **For hair**: comb, shampoo

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Spelling *towel* as "towl". Listen: tow-el.
- Sharing a toothbrush — never share it; it spreads germs.

steps.title: Make a picture dictionary
steps.body: Draw and label these words in your notebook: soap, toothbrush, towel, comb, bath, water.

items.say: soap. Wash your hands with soap.
toothbrush. I use my toothbrush twice a day.
towel. Dry your face with a towel.
comb. She tidies her hair with a comb.
bath. I take a bath every day.
water. Do not waste water.

quiz.why: The picture 🧼 shows 'soap', which we use to wash. A towel, water and bath are different things.

options: a small brush to clean teeth
used with water to wash dirt away
quiz.why: A 'toothbrush' is a small brush to clean teeth. A cloth to dry yourself is a towel.

quiz.q: Choose the word: Dry your face with a ___.
quiz.why: We dry our face with a towel. Water, a toothbrush and a comb do not dry.
The picture 🪮 shows a 'comb', which tidies hair.

quiz.q: Which spelling is correct? (the word for: 🛁 washing the whole body)
quiz.why: Washing the whole body is a 'bath', spelled b-a-t-h. Say it slowly and write each sound.

options: used with water to wash dirt away
a clear liquid we drink and wash with
quiz.why: 'Water' is a clear liquid we drink and wash with. Soap is used with water to wash dirt away.

lessons.title: Sounds and letters: Sounds e, f, g, h

scenes.text: A hen wears a hat and holds a gift.
A frog and a fish clap: "Happy birthday, Hen!"

steps.title: Sounds e, f, g, h
steps.body:
- **e** says /e/ as in *egg*
- **f** says /f/ as in *fish*
- **g** says /g/ as in *goat*
- **h** says /h/ as in *hat*

Big and small: E e, F f, G g, H h.

steps.title: Solved example: blending sounds
steps.body: Say **egg 🥚** slowly, sound by sound, then say it fast. Listen for the 'e' sound.

steps.title: Solved example: odd one out
steps.body:
Which is the odd one out: egg 🥚, elephant 🐘, fish 🐟?

- Step 1: Say each word slowly.
- Step 2: 'egg 🥚' and 'elephant 🐘' share the 'e' sound.
- Answer: **fish 🐟** is the odd one out.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- The **h** sound is just a breath: /h/. Do not say "huh-at".
- Mixing **f** and **p**: for /f/ your top teeth touch your lip.

steps.title: Play I-spy
steps.body: Play 'I spy with my little eye something with the sound…' using the sounds e, f, g, h.

activity.prompt: Sort the words by their sound

quiz.q: Which word begins with the 'e' sound?
quiz.why: 'Egg' begins with the short 'e' sound. Frog, fish and hat begin with f and h.
'Fish' starts with the 'f' sound. Say it slowly and listen to the first sound.

quiz.q: Which word begins with the 'g' sound?
quiz.why: 'Goat' begins with the 'g' sound. Fan, elbow and hen begin with other sounds.
'Hat' starts with the 'h' sound. Say 'h-h-hat'.

quiz.q: Which word begins with the 'e' sound?
quiz.why: 'Elephant' begins with the short 'e' sound. Fish, grapes and gift begin with f and g.

scenes.text: Teacher calls out "place!" and the class shouts "school!", "park!".
Then "animal!" — "cow!", "duck!"

steps.title: Naming words
steps.body:
**Naming words** (nouns) are names of:

- **people**: Tinu, mother, doctor
- **animals**: duck, cat
- **places**: home, school, park
- **things**: soap, towel, comb

Ask: *Is it a person, animal, place or thing?* If yes, it is a naming word.

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
Find the naming words: *Tinu has a duck.*

- Tinu → a person ✔
- duck → an animal ✔
- Answer: **Tinu, duck**.

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
Find the naming words: *The soap is in the bathroom.*

- soap → thing ✔, bathroom → place ✔
- Answer: **soap, bathroom**.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Calling action words like *run* or *wash* naming words. They tell what we **do**.
- Missing people's names — names are naming words too.

steps.title: Speak and write
steps.body: Name 5 things in your bathroom aloud. Each one is a naming word!

activity.prompt: Is it a person, animal, place or thing?

quiz.why: A naming word names a person, place, animal or thing. A towel is a thing, but run is an action and happy describes.

quiz.q: Which is the name of a place?
quiz.why: A school is a place. Tinu is a person, and soap and duck are things or animals.

quiz.q: In "The hen is in the garden", the naming words are…
quiz.why: The naming words are 'hen' (an animal) and 'garden' (a place). 'is', 'in' and 'the' are not names.

quiz.q: Which is NOT a naming word?
quiz.why: 'Wash' is an action, so it is not a naming word. Mother, park and comb name a person, a place and a thing.
'Doctor' names a person, because a doctor is a person who helps people.

questions.q: What colour is Bubbles?
questions.why: Bubbles is a yellow rubber duck.

questions.q: What did Tinu use to make bubbles?
questions.why: Tinu rubbed soap to make bubbles.

questions.q: What did Tinu use to dry himself?
questions.why: Tinu dried himself with a soft towel.

questions.q: Which word matches 🪥?
questions.why: The picture 🪥 shows a 'toothbrush', which cleans teeth. Soap, a towel and a bath are different things.

questions.q: Choose the word: Wash your hands with ___.
questions.why: We wash our hands with soap, which cleans away dirt and germs. A comb, towel and toothbrush do not wash hands.

questions.q: What does 'comb' mean?
options: a clear liquid we drink and wash with
used with water to wash dirt away
questions.why: A 'comb' is a tool to tidy hair. A cloth to dry yourself is a towel.

questions.q: Which spelling is correct? (the word for: 🧺 a cloth to dry yourself)
questions.why: The cloth to dry yourself is a 'towel', spelled t-o-w-e-l. Say it slowly and write each sound.

questions.q: Which sound does 'fish 🐟' begin with?
questions.why: 'Fish' starts with the 'f' sound.

questions.q: Which word begins with the 'g' sound?
questions.why: 'Goat' begins with the 'g' sound. Egg, elbow and frog begin with e and f.

questions.q: Which sound does 'hat 🎩' begin with?
questions.why: 'Hat' starts with the 'h' sound.

questions.q: Which is a naming word?
questions.why: A towel is a naming word because it is a thing. Run is an action and happy describes.

questions.q: Which is the name of a place?
questions.why: A school is a place. The others are a person (Tinu), a thing (soap) and an animal (duck).

questions.q: In "The hen is in the garden", the naming words are…
questions.why: The naming words are 'hen' (an animal) and 'garden' (a place).

questions.q: Which habit keeps us healthy?
questions.why: Washing hands before eating keeps us healthy because clean hands stop germs. Sharing toothbrushes, never bathing and dirty clothes spread germs.

questions.q: How many naming words: "Ma put the soap and towel in the bag."
questions.why: The naming words are Ma, soap, towel and bag, so there are 4. 'put', 'the', 'and', 'in' are not names.

questions.q: Case: Tinu forgot his towel. What is the best thing to do?
options: Run out wet and drip everywhere
questions.why: Asking politely for a towel solves the problem calmly. Running out wet, crying or using the curtain does not.

courses.title: Unit 3 · Pets and animal friends
courses.summary: Caring for pets, animal sounds and homes, letter sounds i–l, and using a and an.
outcomes: Talk about pets and how to care for them
Answer questions on a short story
Hear the sounds i, j, k, l
Use a and an correctly
courses.note: topic order may differ by edition

lessons.title: Read-along: Kitty and the ball of wool

story.title: Kitty and the ball of wool

scenes.text: Kitty is a little white kitten. She lives with Grandma.
Grandma is knitting a red scarf. A ball of wool rolls off her lap.
Kitty chases the wool round and round the room. Soon she is tangled up!
Grandma laughs and gently untangles her. "Silly Kitty! Here is your own ball to play with." Kitty purrs happily.

steps.title: Before you read
steps.body: Do you have a pet? What does it like to play with?

steps.title: Read the story
steps.body:
Kitty is a little white kitten. She lives with Grandma.

Grandma is knitting a red scarf. A ball of wool rolls off her lap.

Kitty chases the wool round and round the room. Soon she is tangled up!

Grandma laughs and gently untangles her. "Silly Kitty! Here is your own ball to play with." Kitty purrs happily.
steps.say:
Kitty is a little white kitten. She lives with Grandma.

Grandma is knitting a red scarf. A ball of wool rolls off her lap.

Kitty chases the wool round and round the room. Soon she is tangled up!

Grandma laughs and gently untangles her. "Silly Kitty! Here is your own ball to play with." Kitty purrs happily.

steps.title: Solved example: finding an answer in the story
steps.body:
Question: *What was Grandma knitting?*

- Find the line: "Grandma is knitting a red scarf."
- Answer: **a red scarf**.

steps.title: Solved example: what happened first, next, last
steps.body: Order: wool rolls off → Kitty chases it → Kitty gets tangled → Grandma untangles her → Kitty gets her own ball.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Guessing the answer without looking back at the story. Find the line that tells you.
- Reading word by word without thinking about the meaning — read the sentence again as a whole.
- Answering with one word when the question says "why" — give a reason with "because".

steps.title: Talk about it
steps.body: How should we treat pets? Say two kind things you can do for an animal.

activity.prompt: Put the story events in order
items: The wool rolls off her lap
Grandma gives Kitty her own ball

quiz.why: Kitty is a little white kitten, so the colour is white.
Kitty lives with Grandma, as the story says.
A ball of wool rolled off Grandma's lap, which Kitty then chased.

quiz.q: What happened when Kitty chased the wool?
quiz.why: Kitty chased the wool round and round and got tangled up in it.
Grandma laughed kindly and gently untangled Kitty. She was not angry.

lessons.title: Word power: pets and their sounds

steps.title: a and an
steps.body:
We use **a** or **an** before one thing.

- **an** before words starting with a vowel sound: **a, e, i, o, u** → *an apple, an egg, an ink pot, an owl, an umbrella*
- **a** before other sounds → *a cat, a kite, a dog*

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
___ owl

- *owl* starts with **o**, a vowel.
- Answer: **an owl**.

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
___ rabbit

- *rabbit* starts with **r**, not a vowel.
- Answer: **a rabbit**.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Saying *a apple* — it is **an apple**.
- Using a/an with many things (an apples ✘).

steps.title: Speak and write
steps.body: Look around and say 5 things with a or an: a door, an eraser…

activity.prompt: a or an?

quiz.why: Use 'an' before a word that starts with a vowel sound, and 'apple' starts with a. So it is 'an apple'.
Use 'a' before a word that starts with a consonant, and k is not a vowel. So it is 'a kitten'.
Use 'an' before a vowel, and umbrella starts with u, which is a vowel. So it is 'an umbrella'.
'An egg' is right because egg starts with the vowel e. The others do not match: owl needs 'an', and dog and egg need different words.
'A parrot' is right because parrot starts with p, which is not a vowel. 'An cat' and 'a apple' are wrong.

steps.title: Action words
steps.body:
**Action words** (verbs) tell what someone **does**.

- The bird **flies**.
- Pinku **eats** a mango.
- The children **run** and **jump**.

Ask: *What is he/she/it doing?* The answer is the action word.

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
Find the action word: *The sparrow sits on a branch.*

- What does the sparrow do? It **sits**.
- Answer: **sits**.

steps.title: Solved example 2

Find the action word: *Birds sing in the morning.*

- Answer: **sing**.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Picking the naming word (sparrow) instead of the action (sits).
- Thinking "is" is always the action — in "The boy is running", the action is **running**.

A fish swims in water, so the action word is 'swims'. Fish do not bark, read or fly.

quiz.why: 'Mango' is a naming word, not an action. Run, sing and jump are things we do.

steps.title: Describing words: colour and size
steps.body:
**Describing words** (adjectives) tell us more about a naming word.

- **Colour**: a *blue* balloon, a *red* rose
- **Size**: a *big* wheel, a *small* ant
- **Shape**: a *round* plate

They usually come **before** the naming word.

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
Find the describing word: *a big blue balloon*

- big (size), blue (colour)
- Answer: **big, blue**.

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body: Describe a mango: *a yellow, sweet, juicy mango*.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Putting the describing word after: "a balloon blue" ✘ → **a blue balloon**.
- Mixing describing and action words.

steps.title: Speak and write
steps.body: Describe your school bag with 3 describing words.

activity.prompt: Fill in a describing word
activity.text: The elephant is very ___ and the ant is very ___.

quiz.why: In 'a red rose', the describing word is 'red', which tells the colour. 'Rose' is the naming word.
'Tall' tells size, how big or high something is. Run is an action, green is a colour and Ravi is a name.

quiz.q: Which is in the right order?
quiz.why: 'A small kite' is right, because the describing word 'small' comes before the naming word 'kite'.
The opposite of 'big' in size is 'small'. Fast, round and blue are not size words.

quiz.q: Which word describes the shape of a ball?
quiz.why: A ball is 'round', which describes its shape. Sharp, flat and square do not describe a ball.

questions.q: Who went with Ravi?
questions.why: Ravi went to the fair with his father.

questions.q: How does the merry-go-round move?
options: Round and round in a circle
questions.why: The merry-go-round goes round and round in a circle.

questions.q: What colour was the balloon?
questions.why: Ravi had a big blue balloon.

questions.q: Which word matches 🎠?
questions.why: The picture 🎠 shows a 'merry-go-round', a ride that turns in a circle.

questions.q: Choose the word: We saw the city from the ___.
questions.why: We saw the city from the giant wheel, because it is a very big ride that goes up high. A balloon, popcorn and circle cannot carry you.

questions.q: What does 'popcorn' mean?
options: a very big wheel ride that goes up high
a thin rubber bag filled with air
a ride that turns in a circle
questions.why: 'Popcorn' is a puffed corn snack. A giant wheel is a ride and a balloon is a thin rubber bag filled with air.

questions.q: Which spelling is correct? (the word for: 🎈 a thin rubber bag filled with air)
questions.why: A thin rubber bag filled with air is a 'balloon', spelled b-a-l-l-o-o-n. Say it slowly and write each sound.

questions.q: Which sound does 'rabbit 🐰' begin with?
questions.why: 'Rabbit' starts with the 'r' sound.

questions.q: Which word begins with the 's' sound?
questions.why: 'Sun' begins with the 's' sound. Ring, rose and rabbit begin with r.

questions.q: Which sound does 'top 🪀' begin with?
questions.why: 'Top' starts with the 't' sound.

questions.q: Describing word in "a red rose":
questions.why: In 'a red rose', the describing word is 'red', which tells the colour.

questions.q: Which tells size?
questions.why: 'Tall' tells size. Run is an action, green is a colour and Ravi is a name.

questions.q: Which is in the right order?
questions.why: 'A small kite' is right, because the describing word comes before the naming word.

questions.q: Why did Ravi hold his balloon tight?
options: So it would not fly away
questions.why: Ravi held his balloon tight so it would not fly away, because balloons float up. It was not heavy or hot.

questions.q: How many describing words: "a big, round, red ball"?
questions.why: In 'a big, round, red ball' the describing words are big, round and red, so there are 3. 'Ball' is the naming word.

questions.q: Case: Ravi gets lost at the mela. What should he do?
options: Stay where he is and ask a police officer or shopkeeper for help
Go with any stranger who offers sweets
questions.why: If lost, stay where you are and ask a police officer or shopkeeper for help, because they are safe helpers. Going alone, hiding or following a stranger with sweets is unsafe.

courses.title: Unit 6 · Trees and fruits
courses.summary: Why trees matter, a story about a tree and its friends, tree words, sounds u–y and one and many.
outcomes: Explain why trees are important
Answer questions on a story
Hear the sounds u, v, w, y
Change one into many by adding -s
courses.note: topic order may differ by edition

lessons.title: Read-along: The neem tree and its friends

story.title: The neem tree and its friends

scenes.text: An old neem tree stands near the school. Its branches are wide and green.
Squirrels run up its trunk. Birds build nests in its branches.
At lunch, children sit in its cool shade and eat together.
One hot summer the tree looks dry. The children water it every day. Soon new green leaves come out!

steps.title: Before you read
steps.body: Name a tree near your home. Who lives on it or uses it?

steps.title: Read the story
steps.body:
An old neem tree stands near the school. Its branches are wide and green.

Squirrels run up its trunk. Birds build nests in its branches.

At lunch, children sit in its cool shade and eat together.

One hot summer the tree looks dry. The children water it every day. Soon new green leaves come out!
steps.say:
An old neem tree stands near the school. Its branches are wide and green.

Squirrels run up its trunk. Birds build nests in its branches.

At lunch, children sit in its cool shade and eat together.

One hot summer the tree looks dry. The children water it every day. Soon new green leaves come out!

steps.title: Solved example: finding an answer in the story
steps.body:
Question: *Where do children eat lunch?*

- Line: "children sit in its cool shade and eat together."
- Answer: **in the shade of the neem tree**.

steps.title: Solved example: what happened first, next, last
steps.body: Order: the tree gives shade → summer makes it dry → children water it → new leaves grow.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Guessing the answer without looking back at the story. Find the line that tells you.
- Reading word by word without thinking about the meaning — read the sentence again as a whole.
- Answering with one word when the question says "why" — give a reason with "because".

steps.title: Talk about it
steps.body: What can you do to help a tree near you?

activity.prompt: Put the story events in order
items: The neem tree stands near the school
Children water it and new leaves grow

quiz.q: Which tree is in the story?
quiz.why: The story is about an old neem tree. It is not a banyan, mango or coconut tree.

quiz.q: Who builds nests in the branches?
quiz.why: Birds build nests in the branches of the tree.

quiz.q: What do children enjoy under the tree?
quiz.why: Children enjoy cool shade under the tree. They do not play in snow, sand or rain.

quiz.q: Why did the tree look dry?
quiz.why: The tree looked dry because it was a hot summer, when plants need more water.

quiz.q: What happened after the children watered it?
quiz.why: After the children watered the tree, new green leaves came out. Water helped it grow again.

scenes.text: Teacher draws a tree on the board.
Roots, trunk, branches, leaves, fruits — the class labels each part.

steps.title: New words
steps.body:
- 🌳 **tree** — a tall plant with a woody trunk
- 🍃 **leaf** — the flat green part of a plant
- 🪵 **trunk** — the thick main stem of a tree
- 🌰 **seed** — a tiny thing from which a new plant grows
- 🪺 **nest** — a home that birds make
- ⛱️ **shade** — a cool place away from the sun

steps.title: Solved example: using a new word
steps.body:
Word: **tree**

- Step 1: Say it: tree.
- Step 2: Think what it means: a tall plant with a woody trunk.
- Step 3: Use it in a sentence: *A mango tree grows in our garden.*

steps.title: Solved example: grouping words
steps.body: Parts of a tree from bottom to top: **roots → trunk → branches → leaves → flowers/fruits**.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- The plural of *leaf* is **leaves**, not "leafs".
- Thinking roots are useless — roots drink water and hold the tree firmly.

steps.title: Make a picture dictionary
steps.body: Draw and label these words in your notebook: tree, leaf, trunk, seed, nest, shade.

items.say: tree. A mango tree grows in our garden.
leaf. A leaf fell on my head.
trunk. The squirrel ran up the trunk.
seed. I planted a seed in a pot.
nest. The bird made a nest of twigs.
shade. We rested in the shade.

quiz.why: The picture 🌳 shows a 'tree'. A nest, shade and trunk are parts or things connected with trees.

options: a cool place away from the sun
the flat green part of a plant
a tiny thing from which a new plant grows
quiz.why: A 'leaf' is the flat green part of a plant. A nest is a home that birds make, and a seed is a tiny thing from which a new plant grows.

quiz.q: Choose the word: The squirrel ran up the ___.
quiz.why: A squirrel runs up the trunk, which is the thick main stem of a tree. It does not run up a leaf or a seed.
The picture 🌰 shows a 'seed', a tiny thing from which a new plant grows.

quiz.q: Which spelling is correct? (the word for: 🪺 a home that birds make)
quiz.why: A home that birds make is a 'nest', spelled n-e-s-t. Say it slowly and write each sound.

options: a cool place away from the sun
a tiny thing from which a new plant grows
the thick main stem of a tree
quiz.why: 'Shade' is a cool place away from the sun. A nest is a bird's home.

lessons.title: Sounds and letters: Sounds u, v, w, y

scenes.text: A yak drives a van with a violin.
It opens a yellow umbrella when it rains. Wow!

steps.title: Sounds u, v, w, y
steps.body:
- **u** says /u/ as in *umbrella*
- **v** says /v/ as in *van*
- **w** says /w/ as in *window*
- **y** says /y/ as in *yak*

steps.title: Solved example: blending sounds
steps.body: Say **umbrella ☂️** slowly, sound by sound, then say it fast. Listen for the 'u' sound.

steps.title: Solved example: odd one out
steps.body:
Which is the odd one out: umbrella ☂️, up ⬆️, van 🚐?

- Step 1: Say each word slowly.
- Step 2: 'umbrella ☂️' and 'up ⬆️' share the 'u' sound.
- Answer: **van 🚐** is the odd one out.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Mixing **v** and **w**: for /v/ top teeth touch the lower lip; for /w/ lips make a round shape.
- Writing **u** upside down like **n**.

steps.title: Play I-spy
steps.body: Play 'I spy with my little eye something with the sound…' using the sounds u, v, w, y.

activity.prompt: Sort the words by their sound

quiz.q: Which word begins with the 'u' sound?
quiz.why: 'Umbrella' begins with the short 'u' sound. Vase, web and yak begin with v, w and y.
'Van' starts with the 'v' sound. Say it slowly and listen to the first sound.

quiz.q: Which word begins with the 'w' sound?
quiz.why: 'Window' begins with the 'w' sound. Yellow, umbrella and van begin with y, u and v.
'Yak' starts with the 'y' sound.

quiz.q: Which word begins with the 'u' sound?
quiz.why: 'Up' begins with the short 'u' sound. Yo-yo, yak and window begin with y and w.

lessons.title: Grammar and speaking: One and many

scenes.text: One biscuit on the plate. "More, please," says Tia.
Ma gives three biscuits. "Biscuits!" Tia giggles.

steps.title: One and many
steps.body:
One thing = **singular**. More than one = **plural**.

Most words add **-s**: one tree → two tree**s**, one nest → many nest**s**.

Some change: one leaf → many **leaves**, one child → many **children**.

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
One apple, three ___

- Add -s → **apples**.

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
One leaf, many ___

- Special word → **leaves**.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- "Two tree" ✘ → **two trees**.
- "Many leafs" ✘ → **many leaves**.
- Adding -s to one thing: "a trees" ✘.

steps.title: Speak and write
steps.body: Count things at home and say them: one spoon, three spoons…

activity.prompt: Match one to many

quiz.why: To talk about more than one cat, we add -s, so two cats. 'Caties' and 'cates' are not right.
The plural of 'leaf' is 'leaves', a special plural where f changes to v. 'Leafs' and 'leafes' are wrong.
A word ending in -s, like 'birds', means more than one bird. 'A bird', 'one bird' and 'bird' mean just one.
The plural of 'child' is 'children', a special plural. We do not add -s to say 'childs' or 'childrens'.
For many things we add -s, so 'three trees' is right. 'A trees' and 'one trees' mix one and many, and 'three tree' leaves out the -s.

questions.q: Which tree is in the story?
questions.why: The story is about an old neem tree.

questions.q: Who builds nests in the branches?
questions.why: Birds build nests in the branches of the tree.

questions.q: What do children enjoy under the tree?
questions.why: Children enjoy cool shade under the tree.

questions.q: Which word matches 🍃?
questions.why: The picture 🍃 shows a 'leaf', the flat green part of a plant. A trunk is the thick stem and a seed grows into a plant.

questions.q: Choose the word: A mango ___ grows in our garden.
questions.why: 'A mango tree grows in our garden' makes sense, because a tree is what grows mangoes. A nest, seed or trunk alone does not fit.

questions.q: What does 'seed' mean?
options: a tall plant with a woody trunk
a tiny thing from which a new plant grows
the thick main stem of a tree
a cool place away from the sun
questions.why: A 'seed' is a tiny thing from which a new plant grows. A tree is a tall plant, the trunk is the thick stem and shade is a cool place.

questions.q: Which spelling is correct? (the word for: 🪵 the thick main stem of a tree)
questions.why: The thick main stem of a tree is the 'trunk', spelled t-r-u-n-k. Say it slowly and write each sound.

questions.q: Which sound does 'van 🚐' begin with?
questions.why: 'Van' starts with the 'v' sound. Say it slowly and listen to the first sound.

questions.q: Which word begins with the 'w' sound?
questions.why: 'Window' begins with the 'w' sound. Van, yo-yo and violin begin with v and y.

questions.q: Which sound does 'yak 🐂' begin with?
questions.why: 'Yak' starts with the 'y' sound.

questions.q: One cat, two ___
questions.why: To talk about more than one cat, add -s, so 'cats'.

questions.q: One leaf, many ___
questions.why: The plural of 'leaf' is 'leaves', a special plural.

questions.q: Which means more than one?
questions.why: 'Birds' ends in -s, so it means more than one bird.

questions.q: Why did new leaves grow on the tree?
questions.why: New leaves grew because the children watered the tree, and water helps plants grow.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.why: 'Children' is the plural of child and 'seeds' is the plural of seed, with two seeds. So 'The children planted two seeds.' is right.

questions.q: Assertion: Trees give us shade. Reason: Their leaves block sunlight.
options: Both true and the reason explains the assertion
questions.why: Both are true: trees give us shade, and their leaves block sunlight, which makes the shade. So the reason explains the assertion.

courses.title: Unit 7 · Kites, wind and sky
courses.summary: Flying kites on a windy day, sky words, short a and short e sounds in three-letter words, and this/that.
outcomes: Use sky and weather words
Read a story and say why things happened
Read short-a and short-e words
Use this and that correctly
courses.note: topic order may differ by edition

scenes.text: Sundar makes a red kite with paper, sticks and a long string.
On a windy day he runs on the terrace. The wind lifts the kite high.
Oh no! The kite gets stuck on a tree branch.
His uncle uses a long stick to free it, safely, from the ground. Sundar says, "Thank you, Chacha!" and flies it again, far from the trees and wires.

steps.title: Before you read
steps.body: Have you ever flown a kite? What do you need to fly one?

steps.title: Read the story
steps.body:
Sundar makes a red kite with paper, sticks and a long string.

On a windy day he runs on the terrace. The wind lifts the kite high.

Oh no! The kite gets stuck on a tree branch.

His uncle uses a long stick to free it, safely, from the ground. Sundar says, "Thank you, Chacha!" and flies it again, far from the trees and wires.
steps.say:
Sundar makes a red kite with paper, sticks and a long string.

On a windy day he runs on the terrace. The wind lifts the kite high.

Oh no! The kite gets stuck on a tree branch.

His uncle uses a long stick to free it, safely, from the ground. Sundar says, "Thank you, Chacha!" and flies it again, far from the trees and wires.

steps.title: Solved example: finding an answer in the story
steps.body:
Question: *Why did the kite go up?*

- Line: "The wind lifts the kite high."
- Answer: **because the wind lifted it**.

steps.title: Solved example: what happened first, next, last
steps.body: First Sundar made the kite, next he flew it, then it got stuck, last his uncle freed it.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Guessing the answer without looking back at the story. Find the line that tells you.
- Reading word by word without thinking about the meaning — read the sentence again as a whole.
- Answering with one word when the question says "why" — give a reason with "because".

steps.title: Talk about it
steps.body: Where is a safe place to fly a kite? (Hint: away from wires and roads.)

activity.prompt: Put the story events in order
items: He flies it on a windy day
The kite gets stuck in a tree

quiz.why: Sundar's kite was red, as the story says.
The wind lifted the kite up into the sky. A kite flies when the wind pushes it.

quiz.q: Where did the kite get stuck?
quiz.why: The kite got stuck on a tree branch, as the story says.
His uncle (Chacha) helped Sundar get the kite down.

quiz.q: Where is it safe to fly a kite?
options: In an open place away from wires
quiz.why: It is safe to fly a kite in an open place away from wires. Roof edges, busy roads and electric wires are dangerous.

scenes.text: Mina looks up: white clouds, a yellow sun, a flying bird.
And far away — an aeroplane!

steps.title: New words
steps.body:
- 🪁 **kite** — a paper toy that flies on a string
- 🌬️ **wind** — moving air
- ☁️ **cloud** — a white or grey shape in the sky
- ☀️ **sun** — the bright star that gives us light
- 🧵 **string** — a long thin thread
- ✈️ **aeroplane** — a flying machine that carries people

steps.title: Solved example: using a new word
steps.body:
Word: **kite**

- Step 1: Say it: kite.
- Step 2: Think what it means: a paper toy that flies on a string.
- Step 3: Use it in a sentence: *My kite flew very high.*

steps.title: Solved example: grouping words
steps.body:
- **In the sky**: sun, moon, stars, clouds, birds, aeroplane
- **Weather**: windy, sunny, rainy, cloudy

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Spelling *cloud* as "clowd": it is **c-l-o-u-d**.
- Flying kites with glass-coated (manja) thread — it is dangerous for birds and people.

steps.title: Make a picture dictionary
steps.body: Draw and label these words in your notebook: kite, wind, cloud, sun, string, aeroplane.

items.say: kite. My kite flew very high.
wind. The wind blew my hat away.
cloud. A big cloud covered the sun.
sun. The sun rises in the morning.
string. Hold the string tight.
aeroplane. An aeroplane flew over our house.

quiz.why: The picture 🪁 shows a 'kite', a paper toy that flies on a string. A string is the thread, and an aeroplane is a flying machine.

options: a paper toy that flies on a string
the bright star that gives us light
a white or grey shape in the sky
quiz.why: 'Wind' means moving air. A kite is a paper toy, the sun is a star and a cloud is a shape in the sky.

quiz.q: Choose the word: A big ___ covered the sun.
quiz.why: 'A big cloud covered the sun' makes sense, because a cloud can hide the sun. Wind, sun and string cannot cover the sun.
The picture ☀️ shows the 'sun', the bright star that gives us light.

quiz.q: Which spelling is correct? (the word for: 🧵 a long thin thread)
quiz.why: A long thin thread is a 'string', spelled s-t-r-i-n-g. Say it slowly and write each sound.

options: a white or grey shape in the sky
a flying machine that carries people
the bright star that gives us light
quiz.why: An 'aeroplane' is a flying machine that carries people. A cloud is a shape in the sky and the sun is a star.

lessons.title: Sounds and letters: Short a and short e words

scenes.text: A hen has a pen and a map.
A cat on a mat naps by a fan.

steps.title: Short a and short e words
steps.body:
Three-letter words have a **middle vowel**.

- Short **a**: c-**a**-t, b-**a**-t, m-**a**-p
- Short **e**: h-**e**-n, p-**e**-n, n-**e**-t

Blend: say each sound, then join them quickly.

steps.title: Solved example: blending sounds
steps.body:
Blend **c-a-t**:

- /k/ … /a/ … /t/
- Faster: /k-a-t/
- Word: **cat**.

steps.title: Solved example: odd one out
steps.body:
Which is the odd one out: cat 🐱, bat 🦇, hen 🐔?

- Step 1: Say each word slowly.
- Step 2: 'cat 🐱' and 'bat 🦇' share the 'short a' sound.
- Answer: **hen 🐔** is the odd one out.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Reading *pen* as *pan* — listen to the middle sound.
- Guessing a word from its first letter only; read all three sounds.

steps.title: Play I-spy
steps.body: Play 'I spy with my little eye something with the sound…' using the sounds short a, short e.

activity.prompt: Sort the words by their sound

quiz.q: Which word has the 'short a' sound?
quiz.why: 'Cat' has the short 'a' sound. Hen, net and pen have the short 'e' sound.

quiz.q: Which of these sounds do you hear in 'hen 🐔'?
quiz.why: 'Hen' has the short 'e' sound, as in 'e-gg'. It does not have the short 'a'.

quiz.q: Which word has the 'short a' sound?
quiz.why: 'Bat' has the short 'a' sound. Pen, hen and bed have the short 'e'.

quiz.q: Which of these sounds do you hear in 'pen 🖊️'?
quiz.why: 'Pen' has the short 'e' sound. It is not the short 'a' as in 'cat'.

quiz.q: Which word has the 'short a' sound?
quiz.why: 'Map' has the short 'a' sound. Pen, bed and net have the short 'e'.

lessons.title: Grammar and speaking: this and that

scenes.text: Ria holds a mango: "This is a mango."
She points up: "That is the moon!"

steps.title: this and that
steps.body:
- **this** — for one thing **near** you: *This is my pencil.*
- **that** — for one thing **far** from you: *That is a kite in the sky.*
- For many: **these** (near), **those** (far).

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
The kite is high in the sky. ___ is a kite.

- Far away → **That**.

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body:
I hold a ball in my hand. ___ is a ball.

- Near → **This**.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Using *this* for something far away.
- "This are…" ✘ → **These are** for many.

steps.title: Speak and write
steps.body: Point and say: "This is my nose. That is the door."

activity.prompt: this or that?

quiz.why: Use 'that' for one thing that is far away, like the sun. 'This' is for near and 'these' and 'those' are for many.
Use 'this' for one thing that is near, like a bag in your hand.
Use 'these' for many things that are near, like shoes next to you ('are' goes with many).

quiz.q: ___ are birds in the sky. (far, many)
quiz.why: Use 'those' for many things that are far away, like birds in the sky.
'This is a cat' is right because 'this' goes with 'is' for one thing. 'These is' and 'This are' do not match.

questions.q: What colour was the kite?
questions.why: Sundar's kite was red.

questions.q: What lifted the kite?
questions.why: The wind lifted the kite.

questions.q: Where did the kite get stuck?
questions.why: The kite got stuck on a tree branch.

questions.q: Which word matches 🌬️?
questions.why: The picture 🌬️ shows 'wind', which is moving air. A kite flies on the wind.

questions.q: Choose the word: My ___ flew very high.
questions.why: 'My kite flew very high' makes sense. A kite is what flies high on a string.

questions.q: What does 'sun' mean?
options: a flying machine that carries people
a paper toy that flies on a string
the bright star that gives us light
a white or grey shape in the sky
questions.why: The 'sun' is the bright star that gives us light. A kite is a paper toy and an aeroplane is a flying machine.

questions.q: Which spelling is correct? (the word for: ☁️ a white or grey shape in the sky)
questions.why: A white or grey shape in the sky is a 'cloud', spelled c-l-o-u-d. Say it slowly and write each sound.

questions.q: Which of these sounds do you hear in 'hen 🐔'?
questions.why: 'Hen' has the short 'e' sound.

questions.q: Which word has the 'short a' sound?
questions.why: 'Bat' has the short 'a' sound. Net, hen and pen have the short 'e'.

questions.q: Which of these sounds do you hear in 'pen 🖊️'?
questions.why: 'Pen' has the short 'e' sound.

questions.q: ___ is the sun. (far away)
questions.why: Use 'that' for one thing far away, like the sun.

questions.q: ___ is my bag. (in my hand)
questions.why: Use 'this' for one thing that is near, like a bag in your hand.

questions.q: ___ are my shoes. (near, many)
questions.why: Use 'these' for many things that are near, like shoes next to you.

questions.q: Why did Sundar's uncle free the kite from the ground with a stick?
options: Because climbing the tree could be unsafe
questions.why: The uncle used a stick because climbing the tree could be unsafe, so safety comes first. He did not want to break the kite.

questions.q: Which word has a different middle sound?
questions.why: 'Pen' has the short 'e' sound, while bat, cat and map have the short 'a'. So pen has the different middle sound.

questions.q: Choose: "___ clouds over there are grey."
questions.why: Use 'those' for clouds that are far away and many, 'over there'. 'That' is for one thing and 'these' is for near.

courses.title: Unit 8 · Little creatures
courses.summary: Small animals like turtles, ants and mosquitoes, a story about teamwork, short i, o, u words, and in/on/under.

lessons.title: Read-along: The ants and the big leaf

story.title: The ants and the big leaf

scenes.text: A line of ants is carrying food to their hill.
Suddenly rain begins. Big drops fall like stones for the tiny ants!
The smallest ant, Chhotu, finds a big leaf. "Come under here, everyone!"
All the ants hold the leaf together like an umbrella and walk home safely. "Together we are strong!"

steps.title: Before you read
steps.body: Have you watched ants walking in a line? Where do you think they go?

steps.title: Read the story
steps.body:
A line of ants is carrying food to their hill.

Suddenly rain begins. Big drops fall like stones for the tiny ants!

The smallest ant, Chhotu, finds a big leaf. "Come under here, everyone!"

All the ants hold the leaf together like an umbrella and walk home safely. "Together we are strong!"
steps.say:
A line of ants is carrying food to their hill.

Suddenly rain begins. Big drops fall like stones for the tiny ants!

The smallest ant, Chhotu, finds a big leaf. "Come under here, everyone!"

All the ants hold the leaf together like an umbrella and walk home safely. "Together we are strong!"

steps.title: Solved example: finding an answer in the story
steps.body:
Question: *What did Chhotu find?*

- Line: "Chhotu finds a big leaf."
- Answer: **a big leaf**.

steps.title: Solved example: what happened first, next, last
steps.body: The ants carry food → rain starts → Chhotu finds a leaf → they walk home under it together.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Guessing the answer without looking back at the story. Find the line that tells you.
- Reading word by word without thinking about the meaning — read the sentence again as a whole.
- Answering with one word when the question says "why" — give a reason with "because".

steps.title: Talk about it
steps.body: When did your family or friends work together to finish a job?

activity.prompt: Put the story events in order
items: The ants hold the leaf together

quiz.why: The ants were carrying food to their hill, as the story says.
Rain started suddenly in the story.
Chhotu, the smallest ant, found the leaf. It shows that even a small one can help.

quiz.q: How did they use the leaf?
options: As a boat to sail away
quiz.why: The ants held the leaf over themselves like an umbrella to keep dry. They did not eat it or use it as a bed.
The lesson is that together we are strong, since the ants worked as a team to stay safe.

scenes.text: With a magnifying glass, Arun looks closely.
He sees a ladybird, an ant, a snail and a butterfly!

steps.title: New words
steps.body:
- 🐜 **ant** — a tiny insect that lives in groups
- 🐢 **turtle** — a slow animal with a hard shell
- 🦟 **mosquito** — a small insect that bites and can spread illness
- 🐌 **snail** — a slow creature that carries its shell
- 🦋 **butterfly** — an insect with colourful wings
- 🐞 **ladybird** — a small red beetle with black spots

steps.title: Solved example: using a new word
steps.body:
Word: **ant**

- Step 1: Say it: ant.
- Step 2: Think what it means: a tiny insect that lives in groups.
- Step 3: Use it in a sentence: *An ant can carry big crumbs.*

steps.title: Solved example: grouping words
steps.body:
- **Insects** (6 legs): ant, mosquito, butterfly, ladybird
- **Not insects**: snail (no legs), turtle (4 legs), spider (8 legs)

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Spelling *mosquito* — m-o-s-q-u-i-t-o.
- Leaving water standing in pots — mosquitoes breed in still water; empty it out.

steps.title: Make a picture dictionary
steps.body: Draw and label these words in your notebook: ant, turtle, mosquito, snail, butterfly, ladybird.

items.say: ant. An ant can carry big crumbs.
turtle. The turtle hides in its shell.
mosquito. A mosquito buzzed near my ear.
snail. The snail left a shiny trail.
butterfly. A butterfly sat on a flower.
ladybird. The ladybird has six legs.

quiz.why: The picture 🐜 shows an 'ant', a tiny insect that lives in groups.

options: a slow creature that carries its shell
a small red beetle with black spots
a slow animal with a hard shell
quiz.why: A 'turtle' is a slow animal with a hard shell. A snail is also slow but is a creature that carries its shell, and a ladybird is an insect.

quiz.q: Choose the word: A ___ buzzed near my ear.
quiz.why: A mosquito buzzes near our ear, so 'A mosquito buzzed near my ear' makes sense. The other animals do not buzz like that.
The picture 🐌 shows a 'snail', a slow creature that carries its shell.

quiz.q: Which spelling is correct? (the word for: 🦋 an insect with colourful wings)
quiz.why: An insect with colourful wings is a 'butterfly', spelled b-u-t-t-e-r-f-l-y. Say it slowly and write each sound.

options: a slow animal with a hard shell
a small insect that bites and can spread illness
a small red beetle with black spots
quiz.why: A 'ladybird' is a small red beetle with black spots. A butterfly has colourful wings and a turtle has a hard shell.

lessons.title: Sounds and letters: Short i, o and u words

scenes.text: A fox sits in a box on a bus.
A fish in a cup looks at the sun.

steps.title: Short i, o and u words
Solved example: blending sounds
steps.body: Blend **b-u-s**: /b/ … /u/ … /s/ → **bus**.

steps.title: Solved example: odd one out
steps.body:
Which is the odd one out: pin 📌, big 🐘, dog 🐶?

- Step 1: Say each word slowly.
- Step 2: 'pin 📌' and 'big 🐘' share the 'short i' sound.
- Answer: **dog 🐶** is the odd one out.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Mixing short **o** and short **u** (pot/put). Listen: /o/ mouth open round; /u/ short "uh".
- Skipping the middle sound.

steps.title: Play I-spy
steps.body: Play 'I spy with my little eye something with the sound…' using the sounds short i, short o, short u.

activity.prompt: Sort the words by their sound

quiz.q: Which word has the 'short i' sound?
quiz.why: 'Pin' has the short 'i' sound. Pot, cup and fox have the short 'o' or 'u' sounds.

quiz.q: Which of these sounds do you hear in 'dog 🐶'?
quiz.why: 'Dog' has the short 'o' sound, as in 'o-x'. It is not short u or short i.

quiz.q: Which word has the 'short u' sound?
quiz.why: 'Sun' has the short 'u' sound. Fox, dog and lip have the short 'o' or 'i' sounds.

quiz.q: Which of these sounds do you hear in 'big 🐘'?
quiz.why: 'Big' has the short 'i' sound, as in 'i-t'.

quiz.q: Which word has the 'short o' sound?
quiz.why: 'Pot' has the short 'o' sound. Bus and cup have the short 'u', and lip has the short 'i'.

lessons.title: Grammar and speaking: in, on, under

scenes.text: The ball is under the bed!
Now it is on the bed. Now it is in the box!

steps.title: in, on, under
steps.body:
These words tell **where** something is.

- **in** — inside: *The fish is in the bowl.*
- **on** — on top, touching: *The cup is on the table.*
- **under** — below: *The cat is under the chair.*

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body: The turtle is inside its shell. → The turtle is **in** its shell.

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body: The ladybird sits on top of a leaf. → The ladybird is **on** the leaf.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- "The book is in the table" ✘ → **on** the table.
- Mixing *under* with *on*.

steps.title: Speak and write
steps.body: Play hide-and-seek with a toy and say where it is: in, on or under.

activity.prompt: Fill in in / on / under
activity.text: The fish is ___ the bowl. The cup is ___ the table. The cat sleeps ___ the chair.

quiz.why: Milk is inside the glass, so we say 'in the glass'. 'Under' and 'on' would put it below or on top.
A cap sits on top of your head, so we say 'on my head'.
Shoes below the bed are 'under the bed'.
A bird sits on top of a branch, so we say 'on a branch'.
A turtle hides inside its shell, so we say 'in its shell'.

questions.q: What were the ants carrying?
questions.why: The ants were carrying food to their hill.

questions.q: What started suddenly?
questions.why: Rain started suddenly in the story.

questions.q: Who found the leaf?
questions.why: Chhotu, the smallest ant, found the leaf.

questions.q: Which word matches 🐢?
questions.why: The picture 🐢 shows a 'turtle', a slow animal with a hard shell.

questions.q: Choose the word: An ___ can carry big crumbs.
questions.why: An ant is tiny but strong and can carry big crumbs, so 'An ant can carry big crumbs' makes sense.

questions.q: What does 'snail' mean?
options: a tiny insect that lives in groups
a slow creature that carries its shell
a small insect that bites and can spread illness
questions.why: A 'snail' is a slow creature that carries its shell. A mosquito bites and a butterfly has colourful wings.

questions.q: Which spelling is correct? (the word for: 🦟 a small insect that bites and can spread illness)
questions.why: A small insect that bites and can spread illness is a 'mosquito', spelled m-o-s-q-u-i-t-o. Say it slowly and write each sound.

questions.q: Which of these sounds do you hear in 'dog 🐶'?
questions.why: 'Dog' has the short 'o' sound.

questions.q: Which word has the 'short u' sound?
questions.why: 'Sun' has the short 'u' sound. Box has short o, pin has short i and fish has short i.

questions.q: Which of these sounds do you hear in 'big 🐘'?
questions.why: 'Big' has the short 'i' sound.

questions.q: The milk is ___ the glass.
questions.why: Milk is inside the glass, so 'in the glass'.

questions.q: The cap is ___ my head.
questions.why: A cap sits on top of the head, so 'on my head'.

questions.q: The shoes are ___ the bed.
questions.why: Shoes below the bed are 'under the bed'.

questions.q: Why was the rain dangerous for the ants?
options: Raindrops are very big for tiny ants
Ants are afraid of the dark
questions.why: Raindrops are very big compared with tiny ants, so rain was dangerous for them. Ants can see and rain is not hot.

questions.q: Which group has only insects?
questions.why: Ant, butterfly and mosquito are all insects, which have six legs. Snails, turtles, spiders and fish are not insects.

questions.q: Case: Water collects in an old tyre near your home. What should you do?
options: Tell an adult so it can be emptied
questions.why: Tell an adult so the tyre can be emptied, because still water breeds mosquitoes. Adding water or leaving it makes the problem worse.

Then the sun comes out while a little rain still falls.

steps.title: Solved example: finding an answer in the story
steps.body:
Question: *When did the rainbow appear?*

- Line: "the sun comes out while a little rain still falls."
- Answer: **when the sun shone during light rain**.

steps.title: Solved example: what happened first, next, last
steps.body: Rain → sun comes out → rainbow appears → Anu paints it.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Guessing the answer without looking back at the story. Find the line that tells you.

steps.title: Talk about it
steps.body: What do you like to do on a rainy day?

activity.prompt: Put the story events in order
items: She paints it in her notebook

quiz.why: It rained in the afternoon, as the story says.

quiz.q: How many colours did Anu count?
quiz.why: Anu counted seven colours in the rainbow.

quiz.q: What did Anu do with the rainbow picture?
quiz.why: Anu showed her rainbow picture to her teacher.

quiz.q: Which colour is in the rainbow?

scenes.text: A red tomato, an orange carrot, a yellow lemon.
A green leaf, a blue sky, a violet flower!

steps.title: New words
steps.body:
- 🌈 **rainbow** — a curve of seven colours in the sky
- 🌧️ **rain** — water falling from clouds
- ☂️ **umbrella** — it keeps us dry in the rain
- 💧 **puddle** — a small pool of rainwater
- ⛈️ **thunder** — the loud sound in a storm
- 🟣 **violet** — a purple colour

steps.title: Solved example: using a new word
steps.body:
Word: **rainbow**

- Step 1: Say it: rainbow.
- Step 2: Think what it means: a curve of seven colours in the sky.
- Step 3: Use it in a sentence: *We saw a rainbow after the rain.*

steps.title: Solved example: grouping words
steps.body: Rainbow colours in order: **V**iolet, **I**ndigo, **B**lue, **G**reen, **Y**ellow, **O**range, **R**ed — remember **VIBGYOR**.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Spelling *umbrella* — u-m-b-r-e-l-l-a (two l's).

steps.title: Make a picture dictionary
steps.body: Draw and label these words in your notebook: rainbow, rain, umbrella, puddle, thunder, violet.

items.say: rainbow. We saw a rainbow after the rain.
rain. The rain made puddles.
umbrella. Open your umbrella.
puddle. He jumped in a puddle.
thunder. The thunder was very loud.
violet. Violet is the first colour of the rainbow.

quiz.why: The picture 🌈 shows a 'rainbow', a curve of seven colours in the sky.

options: the loud sound in a storm
it keeps us dry in the rain
quiz.why: 'Rain' means water falling from clouds. Thunder is a loud sound and an umbrella keeps us dry.
We open an umbrella to stay dry in the rain, so 'Open your umbrella' makes sense. We cannot open thunder, a rainbow or rain.
The picture 💧 shows a 'puddle', a small pool of rainwater.

quiz.q: Which spelling is correct? (the word for: ⛈️ the loud sound in a storm)
quiz.why: The loud sound in a storm is 'thunder', spelled t-h-u-n-d-e-r. Say it slowly and write each sound.

options: the loud sound in a storm
a curve of seven colours in the sky

lessons.title: Sounds and letters: Sounds sh, ch, th

scenes.text: A chick sails on a ship with a shell.
She eats cheese and gives a thumbs up!

steps.title: Sounds sh, ch, th
steps.body:
Two letters can make **one sound**:

- **sh** as in *ship* (quiet sound: shhh!)
- **ch** as in *chair* (a sneeze: choo!)
- **th** as in *thumb* (tongue between teeth)

steps.title: Solved example: blending sounds
steps.body: Say **ship 🚢** slowly, sound by sound, then say it fast. Listen for the 'sh' sound.

steps.title: Solved example: odd one out
steps.body:
Which is the odd one out: ship 🚢, shoe 👟, chair 🪑?

- Step 1: Say each word slowly.
- Step 2: 'ship 🚢' and 'shoe 👟' share the 'sh' sound.
- Answer: **chair 🪑** is the odd one out.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Saying "s-h" separately — **sh** is one sound.
- Saying "tree" for *three*; put your tongue between your teeth for **th**.

steps.title: Play I-spy
steps.body: Play 'I spy with my little eye something with the sound…' using the sounds sh, ch, th.

activity.prompt: Sort the words by their sound

quiz.q: Which word begins with the 'sh' sound?
quiz.why: 'Ship' begins with the 'sh' sound. Thumb and three begin with 'th', and chair begins with 'ch'.
'Chair' starts with the 'ch' sound.

quiz.q: Which word begins with the 'th' sound?
quiz.why: 'Thumb' begins with the 'th' sound. Chair, chick and shoe begin with 'ch' and 'sh'.
'Shoe' starts with the 'sh' sound.

quiz.q: Which word begins with the 'ch' sound?
quiz.why: 'Cheese' begins with the 'ch' sound. Shoe starts with 'sh' and thorn and thumb with 'th'.

scenes.text: Teacher says "day!" — the class says "night!"
"Hot!" — "Cold!" Everyone laughs.

steps.title: Opposites
steps.body:
**Opposites** mean the very different thing.

- big ↔ small, hot ↔ cold, wet ↔ dry
- up ↔ down, day ↔ night, happy ↔ sad
- open ↔ close, fast ↔ slow

steps.title: Solved example 1
steps.body:
Opposite of *wet*?

- After a towel you are… **dry**.

steps.title: Solved example 2
steps.body: Complete: The sun is hot; ice is ___ → **cold**.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body: - Choosing a similar word (big → large) instead of the opposite (small).

steps.title: Speak and write
steps.body: Act out opposites with a friend: one says "up", the other shows "down".

activity.prompt: Match the opposites

quiz.why: The opposite of 'hot' is 'cold'. 'Warm' is only a little hot.
The opposite of 'up' is 'down'. Top, sky and high mean the same as up.
The opposite of 'day' is 'night'. Noon and morning are parts of the day.
The opposite of 'wet' is 'dry'. Water and rain are wet things, and damp is a little wet.
The opposite of 'happy' is 'sad'. Glad and joyful mean the same as happy.

questions.q: When did it rain?
questions.why: It rained in the afternoon.

questions.q: How many colours did Anu count?
questions.why: Anu counted seven colours.

questions.q: What did Anu do with the rainbow picture?
questions.why: Anu showed her rainbow picture to her teacher.

questions.q: Which word matches 🌧️?
questions.why: The picture 🌧️ shows 'rain', water falling from clouds.

questions.q: Choose the word: We saw a ___ after the rain.
questions.why: 'We saw a rainbow after the rain' makes sense, since rainbows appear when sun and rain come together.

questions.q: What does 'puddle' mean?
options: it keeps us dry in the rain
a curve of seven colours in the sky
questions.why: A 'puddle' is a small pool of rainwater. Rain is the water that falls and a rainbow is a curve of colours.

questions.q: Which spelling is correct? (the word for: ☂️ it keeps us dry in the rain)
questions.why: The thing that keeps us dry in the rain is an 'umbrella', spelled u-m-b-r-e-l-l-a. Say it slowly and write each sound.

questions.q: Which sound does 'chair 🪑' begin with?
questions.why: 'Chair' starts with the 'ch' sound.

questions.q: Which word begins with the 'th' sound?
questions.why: 'Thumb' begins with the 'th' sound. Chair and chick start with 'ch' and shoe with 'sh'.

questions.q: Which sound does 'shoe 👟' begin with?
questions.why: 'Shoe' starts with the 'sh' sound.

questions.q: Opposite of hot:
questions.why: The opposite of 'hot' is 'cold'.

questions.q: Opposite of up:
questions.why: The opposite of 'up' is 'down'.

questions.q: Opposite of day:
questions.why: The opposite of 'day' is 'night'.

questions.q: Which colour comes just after green in the rainbow (VIBGYOR)?
questions.why: The rainbow order is V-I-B-G-Y-O-R, so the colour just after green is yellow.

questions.q: Choose the sentence with a correct opposite pair.
options: The tortoise is big but the hare is large.
The tortoise is slow but the hare is fast.
The tortoise is slow and the hare is slow.
The tortoise is fast but the hare is quick.
questions.why: Slow and fast are opposites, so 'The tortoise is slow but the hare is fast' is right. The other sentences use words that mean the same, or the wrong pair.

questions.q: Case: There is thunder and lightning while you play outside. What should you do?
questions.why: Go indoors quickly, because indoors is safest in thunder and lightning. Flying a kite, climbing a pole or standing under a tall tree is dangerous.

Word: **tailor**

Helper → tool:

- tailor → needle, sewing machine

- cook → pan

farmer. The farmer grows rice.

a person who keeps us safe

options: a person who keeps us safe
